carbon_policy_signal.item: EU loosens ETS rules, allowing industry longer free allocation through 2040s; trilogue negotiations on stringency ongoing.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Reduced EUA scarcity via extended free allocation lowers fossil-power generation's carbon compliance cost, depressing merit-order abatement incentive and coal-to-gas switching margin.

freshness_caveat: Coal (207 days old, as of 2025-12-26) and Clean Dark (202 days old, as of 2025-12-31) are stale; fuel-mix merit-order claims lack current coal/gas parity. Use cautiously in spread analysis.
risk_flags: GB Power 160.85 EUR/MWh (99th pctile) — 13.86% daily move suggests capacity/import shock; watch GB interconnector and renewable forecast.
EU Storage 15.5 pp below seasonal at 54% full (28th pctile) — refill pace into Aug–Sep will set H2 power baseload risk; TTF upside if demand shocks north.
Coal stale (207 days old, 7th pctile at 96 USD/t) — merit order now gas-centric; coal price reset needed for fuel-mix credibility.
Iran-Hormuz tail risk and EU sanctions delay on Russian crude cap (decision end July) could trigger crude spike → HFO burn → indirect TTF substitution pressure.

base.summary: GB supply tightens, TTF holds premium on storage deficit; EUA drifts lower on reform oversupply signal.

downside.summary: US LNG supply surge + cooler forecast weakens demand; EU storage refill accelerates. TTF –5–8%, DE Power –3–6%.

upside.summary: Iran-Hormuz escalation or EU sanctions ratchet tightens crude; HFO burn lifts gas arb; GB capacity shock deepens. TTF +8–12%, DE Power +5–8%.

themes: GB power spike vs coal collapse — fuel-switch regime inverted
TTF extended above trend; storage deficit and geopolitical risk sustaining premium
EU carbon reform loosens scarcity, bearish power spreads
US LNG record exports pressure spot-forward convergence
top_drivers: GB Power spike to 99th pctile (160.85 EUR/MWh, +13.86% daily) — capacity tightness, renewable dip, or import constraint dominating spreads.
TTF extended +2.7σ above 50d trend (58.74 EUR/MWh, +40.15% monthly) — Iran-Hormuz geopolitical premium and EU storage deficit (15.5 pp below seasonal) sustaining gas upside bias.
EU carbon reform loosens ETS scarcity through 2040s — bearish power spreads via lower abatement cost; coal-to-gas switch incentive collapsing.
US LNG record export surge (56.3 Bcf/d in 2025) — raises spot LNG optionality for Europe, convergence risk to TTF front-month, bearish pressure if supply glut.
top_takeaway: GB Power at 99th percentile amid tight EU storage (15.5 pp below seasonal); TTF extended +2.7σ on Iran-Hormuz premium, EU carbon reform bearish, US LNG supply upside risk.

watchlist.why: GB at 99th pctile with 13.86% daily spike suggests supply tightness or import constraint; monitor wind forecast and cross-channel flows.
Currently 15.5 pp below seasonal; pace of withdrawal or injection will signal H2 demand-supply tightness and TTF curve shape through winter.

watchlist.metric: EU sanctions decision on Russian crude price cap
watchlist.why: Delayed until end July; outcome signals escalation or de-escalation and affects HFO/gasoil burn margin and indirect gas substitution pressure.

watchlist.metric: US LNG export growth and spot-forward LNG-TTF arb
watchlist.why: Record 56.3 Bcf/d in 2025 raises European import optionality; LNG-TTF convergence risk pressures front-month TTF and extends downside bias if US supply surge.
EU loosens ETS rules for longer free allocation through 2040s; bearish scarcity narrative reduces abatement incentive and pressures power spreads via lower carbon cost.
